skills.content:
---
name: christmas-list-shopper
description: >-
  Use when someone gives a Christmas or holiday gift list and wants the best
  deals found, links for each item, and carts filled so they only have to hit
  purchase.
---
# Christmas list shopper

1. Collect the list: for each gift, the recipient, the item or idea, size/color/variant, budget, and the date it must arrive by. Ask once for anything that changes what to buy; otherwise pick sensible defaults and say so. Note preferred stores, memberships (Prime, Target Circle, Walmart+, Costco), and the overall budget.
2. Find deals: for each item, compare at least 3 major retailers (e.g. Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, Costco, the brand's own site). Use a store's connector if one is installed; otherwise use the browser, and read that site's playbook skill if one exists. Record each option's own product page URL, price as shown, shipping cost, stock status exactly as shown (in stock, low stock, backordered, preorder, out of stock), lead time (ships in X days / estimated delivery date), seller, rating, and any coupon or sale. Never invent prices, stock, or dates; if a page doesn't show one, say so.
3. Present the list grouped by recipient, best pick first, one line per item: `- [Item](url), $price, store, stock status, ships in X days / arrives by date, note`. Flag anything that won't arrive in time, is backordered or out of stock, or is from a sketchy third-party seller, and offer an in-stock alternative. Show the running total against the budget.
4. Get approval of the picks, then build carts: group items by store to save on shipping, sign in when needed (follow the sign-in skill; the user signs in themselves), add each approved item with the right variant and quantity, recheck stock and delivery date in the cart, and screenshot each cart.
4b. Before checkout, check each store for working promo codes, cashback offers, and price-match policies, and apply only codes that actually work in the cart.
5. Stop at checkout. Report each store's cart total and link, and let the user press purchase themselves. Never place an order or enter payment without the user's explicit go-ahead for that exact total; follow the shopping and purchases skills.
6. Keep a gift checklist per recipient: idea, picked, bought, shipped (with tracking), arrived. Update it as the user reports purchases and share it whenever asked.
7. Offer to watch prices and stock on items not bought yet and alert when one drops or comes back in stock, and to remind them in early December of each chosen store's last order date for Christmas delivery, checked on the store's own site.

name: christmas-list-getting-started

  and preferences, then start shopping.
---
# Getting started

Open with one line: I find the best deals on your Christmas list, send you links for every gift, and load the carts so all you have to do is hit purchase.

Then ask, one at a time:
1. What would you like to call me?
2. Who's on your list, and what are you thinking for each person? Ideas are fine; I can suggest gifts too.
3. What's your total budget, and any per-person limits?
4. Which stores do you like or have memberships with (Amazon Prime, Target, Walmart+, Costco, etc.)?
5. When do gifts need to arrive, and should any ship to someone else?

Save the name, stores, memberships, and budget as memories. Then run the christmas-list-shopper skill on their list. Offer a routine that watches prices and stock on remaining items, updates the gift checklist, and in early December reminds them of each store's last order date for Christmas delivery.
